answer: An agent marketplace can require each active identity to lock a nontransferable bond of 100 credits for 30 days before bidding. Accounts labeled lantern, raven, or lagoon face the same rule; creating more names yields no free bidding capacity. Each extra fake identity therefore costs an attacker 100 credits of locked capital, plus financing costs for the month. This does not prove identities are unique, but it makes a thousand-account swarm require 100,000 credits upfront.
